paragraphs: Rav Oshaya and Rav Chanina were shoemakers in the Land of Israel. They sat in the prostitutes’ marketplace, made shoes for them, and did not look at them (Pesachim 113, beginning of b; Yuchasin gives Kiddushin, first chapter, where I did not find it). Sanhedrin 67b: every eve of Shabbat they studied Sefer Yetzirah, and a third-grown calf was created for them (see Rashi, Haddar 63a). Sanhedrin 14: Rabbi Yochanan wished to ordain them (Yuchasin writes Rav Huna and Rav Hoshaya; he encountered another reading), but it did not succeed because they descended from Eli. Chiddushei Aggadot says to read Rav Oshaya and Rav Chanina, not Rabbi. They were Rabbah’s brothers (see there). Ketubbot 111, beginning of b: they sent that the law follows Rabbi Yehudah concerning mules. Yuchasin attributes to Rabbi Chananel the explanation that, being of Eli’s house, they sent the ruling that one does not consider the father’s seed. This is incorrect: R.Ch. did not say it. Rather Rabbi Yehudah is uncertain, and the rabbis hold paternal seed is disregarded, as Rashi writes; likewise chapter Oto Ve'et Beno (Maharit there). Jerusalem Talmud, Ha'arel, halakhah 3: Rabbi Yosa says that in the future God will attend only Levi’s tribe, from “He shall purify Levi’s sons.” Rav Oshaya asks, “Because we are Levites, shall we lose?” Rav Chanina [ר״ח in Heilprin] and Rabbi Oshaya sat at Jerusalem’s gate; an elder taught them from Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s school, Makkot 19b. The Gemara’s “What is it? It is obvious,” etc.—“What is it?” is an error, as appears in Rashi and in Yalkut, Re'eh. The new Talmud editions did not correct it.
